title: Ranked approaches for outbound event compatibility

masthead.headline: Four complete migration shapes, one invariant.
masthead.lede: Every frame uses the same six consumers, forty-eight-hour overlap, v1-to-v2 contract change, and zero-drop objective. Only the compatibility mechanism changes.

sections.label: Viable set
sections.title: Inspect the mechanism, not just its label.

blocks.text: Each ranked frame below is deliberately complete enough to review: mechanism, live state, owner, rollback, and pressure case. Rankings are suggestions until you explicitly respond.
Each cell carries a judgment against the ranking basis — rollback, then ownership, then the failure it invites. A glyph doubles the colour so the verdict survives a greyscale print.

blocks.title: Cheap probe
blocks.text: Replay one day of production events through a producer adapter and compare both envelopes before committing to infrastructure.

blocks.label: Final ranked direction
blocks.ask: Select one direction after reviewing all four frames.

pros: Reversible by one switch, inside a single sprint.
No new service for another team to own.
cons: Leaves translation logic in the producer, which grows with each consumer.

choices.summary: Keep when long overlap is material.
pros: Each consumer migrates on its own schedule.
cons: Two live schemas to operate for as long as the overlap runs.

choices.summary: Keep only when producer ownership is unavailable.
pros: Needs no change from a producer team that will not prioritise one.
cons: The same translation is written once per consumer, and drifts between them.

choices.summary: Choose when contract negotiation deserves a platform owner.
pros: One place where every contract change is reviewed.
cons: A new service on the critical path, and a team to staff for it.

blocks.recommendation: Take the producer adapter. It is the only one of the four that can be undone inside a single sprint, and nothing we know today tells us which of the other three is right — so the value of staying reversible is higher than the cost of translating in the producer for another quarter.

blocks.label: Rank the steps in the order you would take them
items: Stand the adapter up and prove it against one consumer
Move the remaining five consumers across

blocks.label: Recommended direction
blocks.ask: Approve the producer adapter as the reversible baseline, with the forty-eight-hour overlap and a single-switch rollback, or ask for a change.
blocks.placeholder: For example: hold the overlap open for a week.

blocks.label: Dominant comparison tradeoff
blocks.ask: Which tradeoff should dominate the eventual decision?
blocks.placeholder: For example: support a twelve-month consumer migration window.

blocks.label: Missing shape
blocks.ask: Which migration shape is missing from the ranked set?
blocks.placeholder: For example: dual-write with a reconciliation job.
